This is the TRUE successor to Diablo 2 this is what Diablo 3 should have been. But enough of Diablo and lets talk about Grim Dawn.
2nd Edit (from original that I now removed because I beat the DLC and am now full level)
DLC:
Newly released DLC offers the final portion of the story that was left untold when you beat the original game, it adds several new locations, factions, new quests, new gear, higher level cap, and new potions (respec and others), new crafting equipment, and much more that I'm sure I missed. This new DLC is 100% worth the price (and I am not the one to buy DLC...) but this I have no regrets about at all. New areas to explore and new gear to hunt for and crafting material simply added many more hours for me to sink into this already fantastic game. I highly recommend this to anyone looking for a new/different dungeon crawler that is not a mediocre one like Diablo 3.
This is a dungeon crawler thats main focus is a story and exploration of every map, and when I say exploration I mean hug that wall until you find a secret passage that leads you to a chest as your reward and if you, dont run around again until you do. This game has some of the most creative and beautiful looking areas. I mean thought and detail went into making these maps you wont be dissapointed. As for story I honestly skipped all the dialogue just so I can jump back in to looting and Xp gaining but it was mediocre at best to me, lets be honest story is not the top five reasons we play dungeon crawlers. A nice addition to progression in story though are choices you make with people that you discover while exploring, save them, kill them, rob them its your choice but it has an effect on the game you will either lose a shopkeeper or get a different blacksmith or just lose faction points. Which brings me to the next thing; factions there are many factions to side with and each one carries unique items at the shops. I believe there is only one choice where you REALLY have to choose a faction as in you side with one and the other will hostile you, and every other faction you will always be friendly with so its another thing to do in this game.
Mechanics in this game are really good zero to no issues at all, my only few gripes are when you going up/down curved stairs your character tends to do the opposite of what you want (i.e running into a wall instead of getting up/down stairs) sometimes trying to pick-up loot is annoying you clicking on the item and your character ends up chacing his tail while making laps around the item you want to pick-up and thats prittey much it (there are probably fewe more issues but they are so minor its not worth listing)
Skills: AWWWW YISSSSSS, SO. MANY. SKILZZZZZZ!!! There are many you can pick a class then double up on another class so oin top of main skills there are second class skills and ON TOP OF ALL THAT Devotion points from shrines to make you even more badass.
Items: There are many every one unique in their own way so play around with them all to find whats best for you. (This is for those that played Diablo 2; so there are items in this game that grant you skills outside of the skills you get as whatever class you chose like Enigma for teleporting in Diablo 2 and so on and items now grant you more skill points to particular skills which is also very nice)
So lets sum it all up in simple PROS/CONS;
PROS:
-Graphics: (dark atmosphere, DYNAMIC WEATHER, just that gritty look in general), Detailed textures
-Items
-GORE (Oh yes, there is a lot of blood and pieces of your fallen enemies that will fly around the screen
-Skills
-Level design
-Quests are very well done
-Factions
-Crafting
-Exploring and rewards for exploring
-Unique enemies (elites/bosses/SUPER BOSSES)
-MOD support AND play with MODS online with friends too!! (assuming they have same mods installed)
CONS:
-Some glitches here and there
-Few annoying mechanical issues (stated above)
-Game can crash in MP when someone leaves/joins session (FIXED BY MAKING GAME IN FULL SCREEN-WINDOWED MODE)
-Drop rate for legendary is really, REALLY low (mods fix that)

This review is ten years late. So is this game's proper sequel.
January 2007. Three weeks after getting a gaming PC and Bioshock for Christmas, my brother bought me the Orange Box for my birthday. Nothing could have prepared me for a collection of Valve's finest games that still hold solid today.
Half Life 2 caught my attention immediately, it was a game that I heard a lot about for two years. I played it and its two episodes, and was blown away with how a game could be so utterly fantastic in atmosphere, story, and gameplay.
Marc's script is short, but fantastic. After debating for years with friends and fellow gamers on "what would it be" theories, Marc's story is pretty close to what we'd come up with. An engaging story with deep characters and awesome gameplay were in there, and a conclusive end. Maybe not to the Half Life series, but to our hero. The One Free Man.
You can finally rest, Gordon. It's over.﻿

WARNING: Before you read the rest of this review, I would say that this game is worth having, IF, you bought it while it was on sale. The DLC is waaay overpriced, so I would only recommend this game if you can get it AND the DLC you want while it is on sale. And the only glaring balance issue, is that the Soviets are Over-Powered in the Barbarossa theatre of war, because of a complete lack of effective anti-tank cannons on German Vehicles in that theatre. That is my ONLY major complaint on balancing.
Balancing issues have, for the most part, been solved, still a few kinks here and there but every rts strategy game that has more than one faction is gonna have some imbalances. Granted it is low on innovation, but for those who say it is a clone of the first game, they are dead wrong. The soviets function in a MUCH different way than the Americans in the original CoH. As for the difference in squad size, the Russian conscripts are FAR lower quality than the German grenadiers, conscripts aren't effective unless they're in cover, not to mention the German rifle grenades have a much greater range than molotovs, as for german vehicles being op, they were op in WWII, but I would say that in game this is offset by how comparatively cheap Russian tanks are. I will say that, with the exception of the Southern Fronts, the DLC are waaay overpriced, as for buying my own commanders, I don't want to shell out $40 for half a game, but still most games nowadays are $60 brand new, so that kind of offsets it. All-in-all they could've done much worse. The gameplay is fun so I'd rate it an 85-90, but the DLC pricing is annoying.

Ah man, I'm writing this maybe a half-year after I finished the gameplay and I still rememnber how depressing it was. This is a pretty grim game. It may not seem like it at first. But as you play and go deeper, it turns into something dark. I don't want to give away anything but it felt like... no matter what decision you made, things got worse. And you constantly couldn't believe how much worse it would get. You get to the point where you're thinking, "ok, this is pretty crappy. I need someone to toss me a bone here." But no bone gets tossed. No relief. You just get hammered by crushing bad-luck, though in different ways depending on your choices. I only did one playthrough, so I don't know how many other possible consequences there could be. But goddam, there are a lot of hard decisions you have to make in the game. And the game will make you regret those hard decisions, oh believe me. Honestly, I appreciate the change in pace from other decision-based story games. I feel like, with this game, the player doesn't really control the outcome like in other RPGs or story-based games. Rather, the player gets a chance to act like a king (for better or worse) and literally becomes a ragdoll in the world of incredible misfortune. Which is kinda nice for a change but annoying when you really want to control the big picture. But I felt like the writers/directors do not want you to control the overall outcome. Every choice you make is a painful sacrifice that doesn't always lead to something better. Remember that.
So if you're pretty happy with life and need to flagellate yourself emotionally, try this game.

This is a great game, good stratigic aspects, with an amazing storyline. The story is quite long, I'm not really sure how long it is, I was playing on and off, but found it great fun. However, if you are looking for an easy, Blow-the-aliens-up-and-save-the-world type game, this is NOT for you. The game is hard, even on the lower difficulties. I have had this game for a couple of years now and I have completed the storyline. Once. And this was after I had re-loaded saves, after losing most, or all my men. The content is amazing, the way that you play and unlock weapons and updgrades is very clever, and I have found that one of the reasons this game can be hard is if you don't research the right stuff by the right time, meaning that the aliens shoot ahead of you, with you losing a lot of your men, and having a bunch of rookies. The aliens are well designed, however some of them are painfully over-powered, which is exactly how the game should be. It is a real challenge to complete, and you have a real sense of achievement when you complete it. That said, you will probably spend a very very long time on this game, with multiple games, but you will definitly improve, and learn from your mistakes. There are a few bugs and glitches, but not that many, and there are mostly only with view. A couple of times, I have had soldiers die because of mis-clicking and movement which I didn't tell them to do. It was fine. I lived in the end.
Overall, this is a brilliant game, and I would definatly recommend it to those who like a challenge.

FTL: Faster Than Light is a roguelike or rather rogue-lite title that has characteristics of strategy and simulation games. The player is in control of a starship that is fleeing from the powerful rebel forces. The ship needs to get to the fleet command and warn them before it is too late. On your way you come through various randomly generated sectors. You cannot stay in one sector for too long as the rebel forces are closing in on you and take over more of the map every turn.
When I first saw footage of the game I was mildly confused. Was that one screen really all you see during the game? Yes, it actually is. That's not a bad thing, though. In the main part of the screen you always see your ship from above. If there is an enemy ship it will be displayed on the right. While fights are played in real-time the map screen is turn based. On the sector map you can perform one FTL jump per turn to get to a beacon. Most beacons have a random event when you first jump there. That event can be something that just happens, like a sudden fight or something that you find. In most cases however a window pops up and you can choose from several options. Depending on your ships systems, subsystems and crew more options become available. Your ship is equipped with various systems and subsystems. All of those, as well as the ship's raw "attributes" can be upgraded with scrap. You can also use scrap to buy additional systems and subsystems as well as weapons or crew members or just have your ship repaired.
Fights are played in real-time. Luckily you can pause and give orders whenever you want. Every weapon has a certain preparation time before it can shoot and can be aimed at any of the enemy ship's rooms. If a room with a system receives a direct hit that system is damaged and has to be repaired. There is, depending on the weapon, also a possibility for a fire or a hull breach. During a fight you have to micromanage your crew to keep the ship functional. If there is system damage the crew can fix it. They can also repair hull breaches and put out fires. It is however also beneficial to have your crew man certain systems since it raises the particular system's effectivity and the piloting system does not even work properly without a crew member to man it. It is also possible to open and close doors given the door system is working. Opening doors to space can be very beneficial to put out fires or suffocate boarders.
There is a number of races that can all join your crew. Every race has unique characteristics and some of them give you special options in random events. There are various unlockable ship types and layouts for each type. Those don't simply change the room layout but also the starting systems and crew. So your playstyle will not only vary per ship but also per layout.
On the one hand  FTL: Faster Than Light is due to its random generation to a certain extent luck based. On the other hand however there is much room for creativity and strategy. There is a multitude of ship systems and weapons to choose from. Every race has its advantages (and some of them have disadvantages too). There are many meaningful choices to make and if you play for a while you can see yourself getting better every time.
I can definitely recommend this to anybody who likes rogue-lites, strategy or simulation games.

FTL: Faster Than Light is a great game. Be warned before heading in, though. This game is tough. I've put over fifty hours into it and only actually beaten it once. That said the game is extremely compelling and fun.
The power managment system of your ship had me flashing back to when I was a kid watching an episode of Star Trek and hearing the Captain shout "All power to shields, brace for impact!". The Power system can lead to some interesting scenarios, especially when you're in a power draining nebula or your ship has been damaged. Do you put all power to weapons and hope your crew doesn't suffocate from the 02 system being off for too long, or do you put what little power you have into engines in hopes of escaping?
The resource managment is also an interesting mechanic that leads to many important choices. Do you beef up your weapons but leave your ship as tough as the average tissue paper, sink all of your points into armor and have a tank with a pea shooter, or do you attempt a balanced build that leaves your ship mediocre in most areas? Thanks to the randomness of the game you are often helped by random chance scenarios that give you a ton of spare scrap metal or new weapons and mods. Unfortunatly on the other side of the coin you have just as much of a chance that five Mantis warriors will board your ship and tear through your crew and you'll be forced to restart the game.
There are several different ships and ship layouts to be unlocked as well. If you're having too much trouble with the first ship, don't worry. After a couple of runthroughs you'll begin to unlock other alien ships that lead to very different styles of play. If you're doing terribly with the Kestrel Layout 1 then perhaps you'll do better with the Drone heavy Engi ship. The sheer randomness of the game is what helps its longevity, so don't worry if you have a bad playthrough. You'll get a great one soon enough.
Don't let the games difficulty put you off. Even if you never manage to beat this game it is still a ton of fun, and it is always sold at a deep discount during the Steam sales. Do yourself a favor and buy it.

Kinda strange for me to not recommend this game with all the time I've spent on it (though 60-65% of that time has been AFK), but the frustrations outweigh the fun here.
The Pros:
(little over the top for PVP and wars, but it's fun nonetheless)
Cons:
- Everything in this game feels like busywork. The game has tons of things to do, but it just sucks that all of it is tedious and dull; that's why everyone AFKs them all. They have what they call "life skills" which are composed of the most insanely boring things I have ever had to do in any game. Fishing = stand and press space and do some dumb minigame every minute or so to catch something, or AFK it and go have lunch or something. Trading = auto-pathing your horse from one spot to another over and over and over. Gathering = go up to to something and press a button and then wait, then go to another thing and press a button and then wait some more. Processing = literally just decide to process some stuff and watch your character process them while you wait. What is the point of having all this stuff to do in the game if it's all boring and only really for AFKing? I want to PLAY games, not AFK them.
This game is in sore need of some fun minigames and sidequests.
- Most games, if you have the materials for an item, you craft it immediately. Here, you have to wait HOURS, DAYS or WEEKS just to finish crafting something even with all of the materials on hand (unless you pay!). Even something as simple as being able to teleport to the nearest town (the game has no other forms of fast travel), you have to wait 6 hours to do it again? 6 hours? Does this game think I have no other life than it?
- There is ZERO incentive to go to more challenging areas in the game because of how much you have to grind. You could either go to an area that is way beneath you in level and gear and make 5 - 10 mil an hour and a ton of exp, or go to a challenging spot and get 1/4 of that and potentially die. Die, yes, that's another thing: The game punishes PVE death too harshly. You not only lose EXP, but there is a chance of losing gems (some of which are extremely rare and hard as hell to come by). Because of this, everyone 56 up pretty much grinds at the same spot, which creates issues.
- this game is an insane grindfest. Here is what most people do: Find a grind rotation --> grind it --> tell anyone who walks by "Spot taken". Repeat that for hours to lvl up and make money. No matter how good the combat, griding the same enemies at the same spot over and over is a pain.
- this is probably what's going to make a lot of people quit the game. Enhancing gear in this game is not a matter of skill it is a matter of luck; it is all RANDOM. Someone could easily succeed enhancing something their first try, while someoene else could fail it dozens of times. What's worse is that failing to enhance up at higher levels for armor & weapons de-enhances the gear (meaning they go down a level). And worst of all, accessories are destroyed when you fail to enhance them. This system ruins the sense of progression since it isn't based on skill or hardwork, but sheer luck. If you fail, you are left with nothing but wasted money and items and are worse off than when you started. Now it's back to grinding and life skilling. And trust me, you are more likely to fail than succeed when enhancing at higher levels.
- When it comes to pvp this is how it really works: Gear > Skill. Because of this, unless you're fighting someone who's at the same level and same gear stats as you, you will either dominate or be dominated. The effects of the attacks are also too over-the-top that it's hard to keep track of battles involving more than three players.
This is what you will be doing in the game: grind and do life skills to make money and lvl up. You then go and enhance your gear so you can then grind and life skill some more. And if your enhancing fails, you are now weaker than before, so it's back to grinding and lifeskilling. It is just a cycle of doing the same boring things over and over again.

Techland is back at it again but under a new publisher and a new IP, Dying Light. [SPOILERS!]
You play as a man named Kyle Crane, a GRE operative undercover on a island named Harran, that has been infected with a plauge which you guessed it, turned majorty of the folk there into meat-eating maniacs or zombies. So Crane parachutes of a plane and lands only to be halted by 3 raiders in yellow clothing (cough cough Rais Men cough cough) and you some how disarm one of them of there handgun and put one between the eyes, you intimidate the others and take them out in a little cutscene and pass out somehow....I guess. Whatever let's skip ahead to when you wake up all confused on a bed in a huge hotel that where some good people took charge over. You get tasked a job to clear the upper floor, too many infected come you escape somehow and you see "Dying Light" like any game would after a introductive mission they would show the title with sweet music. Anyways I won't explain the whole entire story but if your looking for a good story, click next on your zombie genre quere, the story is awful and is filled to the brim with cliches and being called a ♥♥♥♥♥ by a evil insane cliche villian named Rais atleast 5 times, a strange out of place drug mission and a crappy QTE (Quicktime Event) Final Boss.
However, the best part of the game is it's amazing gameplay, you got the Mirror's Edge parkour, the amazing combat of Dead Island and Dead Island Riptide, a Grappling Hook (Which is my best friend BTW in this game) and Drop kicks. You have an amazing collection of weapons here, as of the 1.12 update, I went through the files to find out there are 453 melee weapons, 40+ firearms, and 200+ Throwing weapons! These all are Sickles to Machetes, to Baseball bats to Katanas there are so many weapons that I couldn't play with every single one! Then like Dead Island, you get Weapon Modifications, but sadly they aren't for Firearms and they aren't as creative as I wish they were but the descriptions are somewhat of a chuckle. But the real fun in the blueprints are the Developer blueprints that are hidden all over the city, like the EXPcalibur or the SICK bomb or the right hand of GLOVa. There is way too much fun to be had here.
The Following: This is where I think Techland lost there minds and just said "♥♥♥♥ it" and took that 10/10 fun scale and just broke it and put it up to 1000/10.  The Following is where improvments are with the Story aspect, gameplay (even though I was perfectly fine with it's gameplay they made it 100x better) and more. The story goes of a man with a fever was telling Lena and Crane about a Countyside and where they can find a cure to the plaque that spread. So Crane goes out there and starts out jumping off a 100ft cliff and going to a farm to meet up with a guy named Jasir, he is a follower of "The Mother" with many others, you try your best to go get some answers but somewhat like the main story you are a errand boy for a while but not too long (Thank god) and yeah won't spoil much but the Ending is so much better, no QTE at all, you use your bare hands to defeat the final boss and there are 2 endings you can go for (3 if you count the secret one) and it is just so much better than the main story and I really think Techland understood there fanbase here (unlike 95% of the developers in this world) So let's get to the gameplay. The new feature they really showed off almost throws the parkour aspect of the game out the window into the public dumpster ready to be collected by a truck. That's not a bad thing though and it makes sense as well, it's a Countryside, not a run down city with 50ft buildings to jump on. They added dune buggys, and holy♥♥♥♥♥♥♥are they fun, you start off with lvl.1 white parts (which are trash) but you get blueprints to upgrade up to Military-Grade lvl.6 platinum parts (which make the damn thing go as fast as a SR-71 Blackbird or atleast that's what it feels like) and as you travel the huge map you get bobbleheads, paintjobs, etc to customize your go to travel machine. Something else that gives me a Walking Dead Dayrl Dixon vibe is the new crossbows, as you rank in the cult from the story you get rewards and the crossbow is one of them, you start off with default bolts and the normal crossbow already fun just with that but it get's better, you will get a upgraded variant you can craft later with elemental bolts (impact, stun, toxic) and it makes it triple the fun.
What can I give the game? I give the basegame a 9/10, a must own for the zombie genre lovers and even ones like me who ignored it for a while, it could of been a perfect 10/10 but for it's terrible story it did have to downgrade positive thoughts of the game, but it's flawless gameplay really kept it up there.
As for The Following I give it a 10/10, a your stupid if you don't buy it rating. Techland improved the gameplay and the story and it is just so amazing I couldn't find any flaw here.
Vinal Verdict:
Dying Light Base Game: 9/10 a Must Own.
The Following expansion: 10/10 a Masterpiece that should be legally required to buy.

The DLC is waaay overpriced, so I would only recommend this game if you can get it AND the DLC you want while it is on sale. And the only glaring balance issue, is that the Soviets are Over-Powered in the Barbarossa theatre of war, because of a complete lack of effective anti-tank cannons on German Vehicles in that theatre. That is my ONLY major complaint on balancing.
Balancing issues have, for the most part, been solved, still a few kinks here and there but every rts strategy game that has more than one faction is gonna have some imbalances. Granted it is low on innovation, but for those who say it is a clone of the first game, they are dead wrong. The soviets function in a MUCH different way than the Americans in the original CoH. As for the difference in squad size, the Russian conscripts are FAR lower quality than the German grenadiers, conscripts aren't effective unless they're in cover, not to mention the German rifle grenades have a much greater range than molotovs, as for german vehicles being op, they were op in WWII, but I would say that in game this is offset by how comparatively cheap Russian tanks are. I will say that, with the exception of the Southern Fronts, the DLC are waaay overpriced, as for buying my own commanders, I don't want to shell out $40 for half a game, but still most games nowadays are $60 brand new, so that kind of offsets it. All-in-all they could've done much worse. The gameplay is fun so I'd rate it an 85-90, but the DLC pricing is annoying.

I have so many STEAM games, that I overlook just how good some of them are. I revisit some of my games, and it is only then that I realize just how good a game is. That's the case with Dying Light. I've had this game since it was first released. I played it a while, and had my attention pulled away by some of my other games. I'm glad I revisited this masterpiece.
There are several side missions for you to do in this big open world. You're free to roam where you want. The play is superb, the running, vaulting and climbing is very fluid. The game looks beautiful. The AI of the zombies is pretty good. The crafting system is deep enough.
Often times you'll be surprised, having one of the undead on top of you with just barely enough time to react. It will all come down to your fight or flight instinct, in several of the situations that occur in this game. You'll need to assess the sitution, and either try to run, or kill.
This is an amazing gaming experience! You can become lost in this scary, and unpredictible world. If you think that the daytime is scary, my God wait till you're away from a safe zone at night! You can find yourself kissing the ground of the safe zones at times, having just escaped from Death in the form of a grotesque humanoid or demonic-looking creature. You and it - looking at one another, seperated only by the razor's edge. You'll realize that you're safe for now, but you'll also quickly realize that you can't hide forever. You'll have to imerse yourself in this nightmare in order to get out alive.
I can't wait to play this through, and then get to The Following. And, when the sequel to this game comes out, look for some record sales.

Alan Wake's American Nightmare is a disappointing spin-off title that feels more like a new episode for the original game than a proper sequel. At least the engine has been upgraded and the controls and visuals are certainly better. This is a good thing too, since American Nightmare is a much more action-oriented game.
Unfortunately in most other ways American Nightmare is an inferior product. It does not have any of the original's atmosphere or tension, the story is rather messy and the game is also quite short. Additionally, there's only three small maps and they are all revisited during the campaign.
It's not a bad game as such, just rather disappointing after the strong original game. Only recommended for big fans of the original or during a sale.
The good:
- Nice visuals
- Improved controls
- Several new enemy types
The bad:
- Weak story
- Rather short
- Lacks the atmosphere of the original
- Only three small maps that are all revisited several times
- Poorly written side characters who don't really seem to fit in Alan Wake's world
- Ammo refills are everywhere and there's no challenge anymore on normal

Yes i still play this game, and probably will for a little while just because theres simply no real rts alternatives.  I do have over 200 hours into the game which shows that its got at least some appeal to it, but my overall experiance has left me swearing more often then not, and i have to acknowledge that the game really is a waste of time overall.
Unit response is so sluggish your units die unneccessarily (and seemingly wait until death is assured), units can magically go into 'miss mode' where you can have 5 tanks shooting at one that is at 5% health that doesnt die no matter how many shots are fired, or unit pathing that really seems to be doing its level best to get your units killed and goes anywhere but where you want, seems to go straight at the enemies needlessly, and exposes units backsides for no reason at all.  Tanks far too frequently need to stop completely and then completele their turns which has a tendency to get them killed.
edit: and with the new tank pathing its even worse, and this is honestly the most unresponsive rts (and maybe game of any kind) in history.  It simply doesnt take commands at certain points or does the worst thing it possibly could when it FINALLY does (like deciding to go in reverse everywhere, which was supposed to be the point of the fix, but they made it even worse somehow).  I wish i was exaggeratting but coh is simply record breaking in how bad units respond or their pathing.  It really unbelievable in scale.
Then there are only 2 factions, and those 2 factions are not balanced very well, and even if they were there are too many one shot kill weapons or things that can destroy your army in a single click which in my opinion goes against everything rts stands for as the enemy cant dodge this attack (see the aforementioned unit response sluggishness) and has no real defense against it except using cheese back on the enemy in turn.
Player stats and much statistics are limited to missing altogether, and they keep removing more information about other players with every patch.  Also this game is THE camping/turtling rts, which is widely regarded as the realm for noobs anyways.
Overall if your desperate for rts in this day and age and HAVE to have your fix and you can find this one sale for $5 then go for it, but overall its a pos and a monument to the failure of the modern video game industry.  Heck even coh 1 seemed like it had more going for it then this game, and you can find mods for it still and people to play against.
Oh and last but not least (altho not limited to, there are certainly other things to gripe about in this game) this is a borderline pay to win game.  If you dont have the pay commanders, prepare yourself to always be at a MAJOR disadvantage.
Really wish this wasnt the only real rts alternative today, and its a bit of a metaphor that relic went under after making it.  Honestly the more i play the i wonder why i havent uninstalled it yet, but a few  weeks later i will be missing standard rts.

This game is free and it is fun, usually.  There are issues, though.
This game has no real cheat detection.  I think that is all you need to know.   Most of the players are noobs who just downloaded because it is free on Steam.  The matchmaking tries to put noobs in the same matches, so you don't run in to a lot of cheaters at first.  Once you decide you like the game, you'll get put against wallhackers and aimbotters, the same ones, all the time.  The community will call this 'skill' and say 'git gude', but if you've ever played a video game online before you know what is up.  You'll also see people speedhack when they destroy your explosives or pound on your cube, but they don't make it otherwise obvious.
Experienced players also make new accounts so they can get matched against new players and pound on them.  They call it 'smurfing'.
Pros, I guess:
- It isn't P2W and it is free to play, so that is good.
- You can unlock all the characters and perks through gold earned via gameplay.
- Overall, the community is pretty nice
- The Devs do communicate with the community, but it is a skeleton crew, so don't expect much new content
The game can be fun once you get through the confusing mess of early noob play.  The problem is hit detection on the various characters and some characters move too quickly.  When you see 2 or 3 jumping Sarges completely avoiding explosion damage and auto-healing while pounding your cube, you'll realize this game is broken at the coding level.  Certain classes are also over-powered and have exploits that make them unnecessarily difficult to counter.

Fast, challenging and downright insane.
If F-Zero is one of the fastest racing games, then this is one of the fastest beat-em-ups. With a crazy combination of ball game and fighting, be prepared to strain your concentration when you try to find the perfect moment to hit the ball into your opponents face!
If you never had a reason to be scared of a ball, this game will give you more than one reason!
Graphics:
The graphics are cartoony, gritty and occassionally as crazy as the game itself. Despite being handdrawn, the animation is perfectly fluid. The backgrounds are nice to look at yet not distracting in the least and the color coding makes it always easy to know who has control over the ball.
Music:
Each character got their own voice with a set of yells and noises, the music is a funky set of electronic music perfectly fit for the speed of the game.
Gameplay:
Play story mode and fight one up to three AIs, with or without time limit, with or without teams. Play against friends locally or online. Change tagging to allow instant kills, change speed up to 200km/h with one hit. Hit the ball normally, use special skills that confuse your enemies.
The moment you think you know how it works, change the rules and start from the beginning. This game can't be boring. Ever.
Other:
While the story mode is fun, this game HAS to be played with friends. Ideally by friends that are about as good at it as you.

This game features a alien invaded world. Of couse that sounds like the common typical "alien invasion. End of days." Stop right there. You are wrong. The game itself features a very tactical strategy landscaped game. It comes with 4 difficulties; Easy, Normal, Classic, Impossible. You can also tweak the settings to use other features, such as "Ironman Mode" Which means you play on one continued save. No loading back. As far as the actual gameplay goes, you've got yourself a strategic plament game, sort of like chess. You have to move your troops into the rigth position, every decision you make could very well be your last, and also a game over. You have to upgrade your equipment well enough to fend off the aliens that threaten your race, by researching or crafting weapons and armor to do just that. But of course once you feel strong enough to handle a few minor aliens, that's when the aliens step up their game and throw in some other aliens that could ruin your day, or take out your whole squad with a single blow to each individual member. The very thought of one of your members being gunned and shot down basically has you sitting on the edge of your seat, desperatley hoping that your troop would be able to survive. And if there is no hope you could always flee. But the adventure doesn't even end there. It starts with you. Get this game. 10/10

There are certainly moments where I'm like
, but there are many other moments where the paperthin gameplay mixes with questionable design flaws. I was hoping for something addicting in the vein of
, but I got something more reflecting this price point.
There are 'wind up' mechanics for shooting and tackling. Because tackling and shooting happen so often, I think the 'wind up' breaks the flow of the game, but that's probably just me. There is also this weird sidedness to tackling; it is much easier to successfully steal the ball when the opponent is going south. Again, not sure if this is intended, but it feels strange. The controls in general can be a bit finnicky. The career mode was a great way to actually add some actual content. You earn money and upgrade your team. In fact, you can't even pass the ball in a predictable way when you start.
+The best humor I've experienced in a game in a long while.
+The artwork is nice; lots of polish.
+Career mode is a great way to keep people playing; I like spending money to upgrade the team.
-Why oh why would you design a game with controller support in mind, yet not have controller support in the menus?
-I cannot stand how slow you move when you are holding the ball. I can't figure out if that was a deliberate design decision to just get you to constantly pass the ball up the field, or just take pot shots at the goal from wherever you are at.
-I am having a hard time getting good 'feedback' from other opponents around me and how they steal the ball from me. They don't have the 'wind up' like I do, so it's strange.
-What if the wind up cone narrowed instead of widening? On paper, that makes more sense to me because you are taking more time to line up your shot AND it would not break the flow of gameplay as much.
It's fun, but I don't see myself dumping in a ton of hours.

The problem with Far Cry Primal isn't that it's a bad action game, but that it's not the game Ubisoft promoted it to be. If you like what Far Cry 3 had to offer and would like a more tribal kind of setting-change, then this would be a game suitable for you. As opposed to hunting Ice Age mammals and taming all sorts of prehistoric beasts that this game is advertising, 70% of the time, you would instead be spending your time in the story fighting off rival tribes the likes of enemy human mobs in the earlier Far Cry games. 10,000 B.C., in this case, is no more special to look at than another action or even an FPS game killing humans.
So unfortunately, this feels more like a template of what could've been a great game, an unpolished prototype with some interesting moments, but ultimately fleeting. You'd be better off waiting for a Blood Dragon-ish expansion pack or even a Far Cry 6 to see if Ubisoft bother to improve upon this game's design, but I wouldn't hold my breath, considering Ubi's recent record bearing similarities with the worst company in America.
You could actually notice that you're in for a bad time early on in the game, when most of the cool action scenes were played out in cutscenes, rather than interactable moments when you could personally fight off that saber-tooth cat (yes, cat, not tiger; there is no such thing as a "saber-tooth tiger"), or even mash some QTE buttons to at least feel like you have anything at all to do with those scenes. The fact that such dramatic action scenes were played out as cinematic cutscenes took away the tension, making me feel like I was sitting on one side watching passively and bored. Of course, this only occurred during parts of the early missions. I have yet to tread deeper, so there might have been some kind of redemption for this ugly flaw. And yet it was a good warning sign to heed me what I've wasted 40 bucks on.
What is probably the most innovative step into video games set in the stone age has turned out to be a real disappointment. Looks like we'll have to settle for those boring RTS games to really play out prehistory.

Chase me, chase me!  I’ve always told my kids ‘you can’t be chased if you don’t run’...but in Dying Light there’s nothing quite like the feral scream of newly minted zombies racing toward you, arms flailing as they rapidly zero-in on your position – or a nighttime cuddle from a volatile as you fumble for your UV light....soooo RUN it is!
I haven’t felt that thrill of being chased for years; where you can almost feel the hands reaching for your shoulder as you sprint up and over obstacles, and then the immense relief landing in a safe house.  Ahhh bliss.  There is real sense of terror when it gets dark and it’s pretty frightening.  Shortly after playing one night, I stepped out on my deck and felt an eerie sense of something lurking just beyond the light.  I admit I was a bit freaked out by the volatiles am still reluctant to go into their nests.
During those intense swarms, flight is sometimes the best course of action but is also preferable when the weapons crap out mid-scuffle, which happens a lot.  Grappling with parkour is a really fun way to get around and avoid those baddies and to explore.  However I found the over-abundance of weapon changes, along with multiple menus for upgrading, blueprinting, creating, repairing, okaying, entering, confirming, extremely time-consuming and frustrating.   Even 80 hours in, the process of crafting, sorting, and equipping is tiresome and takes you out of the game, forcing decisions about things you don’t necessarily care about.  I usually stuck with a few effective favs just to avoid leaving gameplay for extended periods of time.
I was pleasantly surprised at how seamless co-op worked; where we could join/drop on a whim with no disruption to the other.  The two of us enjoyed completing the various fetch and carry tasks while watching each other’s backs while picking locks.  I had hoped for a later skill that would simplify some tasks, such as the lock-picking, automatically crafting medical kits, providing an ability to pick up and throw any object, obtaining goodies without opening each and every cupboard, locker, basket, etc. -- but no such luck.   We could spend hours just ransacking an area, then crafting, shuffling backpacks, changing inventories, etc. before actually moving ahead with the game; I can’t stress how monotonous it became later in the story.
Other than the cumbersome menus, Dying Light has so much more to offer than Dead Island; the zombie NPCs are scary, the open environment is pretty spectacular, and the story is more immersive.  There are times when the fetch/carry and looting seems formulaic but overall the story moves enough to keep things fresh. Even though the main protagonist seems wooden at times, his character works because he’s in a multicultural crazy world where the NPCs provide more richness to the story.
The Following expansion has the added element of driving a tricked out buggy throughout the open countryside.  It’s a fun addition but there are times I miss the rooftop excursions, especially at night.  The quests and storyline in the Following didn’t hold my interest much; I lost track of what was actually going on and didn’t really care.  I just didn’t enjoy the expansion despite the cool buggy, but was eager to go back to the Slums and Old Town to finish some of the missed achievements, and maybe craft something extra special for the occasion.

The short version:
PROS:
1) Probably the best graphics ive seen this year.
2) Good crafting system (mechanics)
3) Great sound effects for the environment
4) Day and night cycle.
5) you can tame and ride animals.
6) i dont think anyone has done a game like this before so points for originalaty.
NEUTRAL:
1) Some good and some very very bad voice acting that reminded me of the madeup language of "the sims".
2) Constant quick events or "mini quests" are good at first but really annoying later.
3) Around every corner something wants to attack and eat you ,which, later in the game is countered by your pet beasts who scare them off but sometimes it doesnt quite work and you endup spending a lot of time fighing off monsters when you are trying to do something else.
CONS:
1) Mediocre story at best.
2) Out of place drug scenes that make no sense
3) Some immersion breaking bugs or game mechanics -super speed animals, clunky terrain at some places where you endup going around the entire mountain just to find the right way and some places where you can clearly jump up are blocked (sometimes you just slide off and sometimes its just not programmed that you can climb there)
4) Melee combat isnt great, everything you hit sounds like a rock and it doesn't feel meaty.
5) Boss fights are immersion breaking and the bosses themselves are bullet, or i guess in this case , arrow sponges, every so often a wave of enemies will spawn and you will have to fight them off if you dont want to die and want to keep fighting the boss which is kind of annoying.
The long version:
For the first 10 hours the game was great and that was that. Afterwards the game fails to introduce anything new or exciting. The story is mediocre at best, only good thing about combat is the bow and the bombs, taming beasts is a good mechanic but its too simple, once youve unlocked the certain beasts you can tame all you need is some bait, it should be harder then that, i mean, you dont just walk up to a cave bear, give him some meat and now he is your best friend bodyguard who would die for you... Some of the game elements make no sense, for example killing a boss ( and you can see that he is clearly dead) only to switch to a completely out of place cutscene where he is still alive. Speaking of boss fights, they are utterly repetitive. Oh and I guess every far cry game now has to have some drug scene except in this game it is out of place and makes absolutely no sense. The core gameplay feels shallow after just 10 hours of gameplay (we have seen it all before) and the main villain is just laughable. On the bright side the graphics look outstanding and the crafting and perk systems and very well done (you can only craft certain things and get certain perks if you have unlocked the corresponding Master). One of the things that gets repetitive after a while is the resource gathering so i strongly suggest putting some perk points towards "resources" which allows you to get more resources per gather point, they obviously tried to fix that with the "resource packs" which you can find at your settlement, but it doesnt quite work due to how much you can hold in your backpack and if you are constantly liberating bases you will run out of them very fast.
FINAL VERDICT:
If you are looking for great immersive gameplay, outstanding combat and story, you are looking in the wrong place. I cant recommend this game...Remember how great was Far cry 3...well comparing this to Far cry 3 is an insult. Buy at your own risk.
overall satisfaction:6/10 .. i shall play never again

The hybrid classes concept actually works, and they did it much better than even on Titan Quest.
Every one of the six classes (now eight) can be played with one, two or even three or four templates you imagine, that you can combine then with the possible templates of the other class, to make your "own template".
You end up with a very different gameplay.
Believe me when I say that at first, skills seem odd, until you discover the true combinations.
I have a Nightblade / Arcanist, with Nightblade as main, who does not use any ranged spell or attack, but uses every Arcanist defense. As an Arcanist is mainly a ranged attacker, this may sound odd, but it actually works.
I have a Nightblade / Soldier, with now Soldier as main, who does not play the same.
I have a Nightblade / Occultist, with Occultist as main, who does not play the same again.
My Occultist is also actually so much different than my friend's Occultist, even if he also plays Occultist as main class.
An important point is that as much as stuff/items have a major importance, you actually choose and define your own template. You also build it the "Diablo 2 way", with skill points you put into skills, which is an advantage in my opinion, as you put more of your own decisions into it along time. This was better, in my opinion, than D3 absence of choice commitment, and Path of Exile loot-based skills.
Attributes (Physique, Cunning, Spirit) are also better made than previous ARPGs, although they would look similar the item requirements are better profiled.
in addition to skill customization in two classes, you also have access to devotion points that you earn along time.
They complete your class templates and powers in the ways you pick yourself.
For instance, for multiplayer I targeted tank survival abilities for my characters, whereas most were looking as DPS classes.

Devotions is a major breakthrough in customization which can be best compared to Path of Exile.
Unlike Path of Exile, devotions are also art and content oriented, and provide a mix of bonuses and a special additional skill. This is more rewarding, in my opinion, than  the sheer stats of Path of Exile larger attribute-map.
Devotions are pathed with affinities (blood, nature, etc) and end devotions require committed choices.
Also, devotion skills can be leveled, like the loot-based skills of Path of Exile.
Take a pistol and shoot at zombies :)
The greatest thing with factions is that, when a faction hates you (really hates you), it will spawn a nemesis to attack you. A Nemesis is a major boss.
Everyone should look for the gameplay which suit their tastes.
I found out the Nightblade melee frenzy suited me. :)
But I also like my soldier heavy two handed legendary punchhammer.
And my occultist indirect engagement.
Or my demolitionist gun pistols and grenades.
With normal, magic, rare, epic, legendary items, and epic and legendary item sets, you have the normal range of loot.
You also have power versions, mythic versions etc of same sets.
As you'll discover, some sets are oriented toward a tclass template or even a hybrid class template.
Many items also provide skills on their own.
And some of these skills are quite superior.
For instance some items give you pets, others give you major strikes, other give you an extreme dodge proc, etc.
And I do not even speak of very rare items here.
Roguelike dungeons are one of the best features especially for multiplayer, where you must adapt yourself to a great challenge.
multiplayer actually adds more role usage (with tanks, DPS etc) than previous ARPGs.
This is because the game can be quite punishing, especially in multiplayer ultimate but even in starting veteran difficulty, to "glass cannon" characters. This is mainly true in multiplayer.
So, instead of tagging along with your friends for no usage at all, and just looting together, you can end up teaming with them for actual roles, as in a great MMO.
There is also great cooperation between players thanks to loot which is not based on your class.
You exchange item sets, relics, you talk about the crafting recipes one has and can do and that you can not do yourself.
Very early on, you can start crafting epic sets in cooperation with your friends.
And you actually will need to in most Ultimate challenges, though not in solo play.
With two click based skills and about 8 active skills on a skill bar, you must choose well your template and item skills.
This reminds me of guild wars 1 limitations ;)
The Crucible is a "last stand" cooperative PVE arena with great challenge and loot.

I had high hopes for this game, being a huge ASOIAF and GOT fan, but was met with constant disappointment in pretty much every episode. While many people will tell you your choices don't matter in a TellTale game, I still found enjoyment in the overall story in their past games and the minor changes that your choices made. This was not the case in Game of Thrones the game.
Plot points are often forgotten, ignored, or just poor in general. The Forresters are uninteresting characters with personalities pretty much lifted from the Starks from the show. The Forresters are stressed to be a pretty minor house in the North, leading one to wonder why several important characters from the show would even bother to take an interest in them. The shoehorning in of characters from the show does little to help the game stand on its own, almost as if the developers believed they had to keep showing characters you actually liked to get you to keep playing.
The ending is easily the most disappointing moment of the game though. I'll refrain from spoilers, but basically none of your choices impact the ending. The greatest impact all of the choices you have made have is simply determining where certain characters are during the last scene. While your choices may lead to deaths for some characters, it's hard to feel genuinely sad over the deaths of people who were barely developed. It also serves as a complete sequel hook which leads to no satisfactory conclusion to most plot points as they're purposely left incomplete in an attempt to get you to buy the next season of the game when it eventually comes out.
If you're a fan of the show/books (like me) I'd still recommend buying this eventually, just when it's on sale for around $7.50 or something. It's a relatively short game and there is little chance you will play it for over 12 hours if you complete on playthrough.

Has it's ups and downs. Although some serious tweeking is needed.
Taking place in the Eastern Front of Europe during World War 2, the game follows the exploits of the Russian Red Army and the German Wehrmacht as they fight it out in numerous historical battles they engaged in such as the battle of Stalingrad, the siege of Leningrad as well as the defence of the outskirts of Moscow.
Gameplay is pretty decent, much like the first COH only with Russians instead of Americans and British armies. Graphics are pretty good assuming you have a machine that can run it. The whole snow and coldness gameplay mechanic is quite a nice addition and the new units and abilities that are introduced are a step up from the first COH. But not much else is added in that department. As I said, it is very much like its predecessor.
The main campaign is a fair length although the story told throughout the campaign is quite poorly done, what with the negative and evil portrayal of the Red Army, somehow making them look more evil than the freaking Nazis themselves rather than the "Company of Heroes" the game title says they are meant to be. I get that the Russians did some terrible things during the war but then again, what military force Allied or Axis didn't? Plus the game kind of goes a bit overboard on the matter. Some of the Russian soldiers and main characters are portrayed rather stereotypically as well not really helping things. I'm not Russian myself but I do see why many Russians dislike this game.
The campaign isn't really great gameplay wise seeing as how the enemy AI acts rather scripted and you can easily predict where they are going to attack and what units they are going to be using seeing as how they use the same unit types over and over again throughout each mission. Then again Relic games have never really been "Excellent" when it came to the campaign.
If you're like me and you enjoyed the first COH games then this might be for you but you won't miss much if you intend to skip it. Overall the game is not great but not terrible either, so-so if you will.
I would like to see the game series continued on different war fronts however. Here's hoping for a COH set in the Pacific anyway.

Here is a quick review about Far Cry Primal.
For a bit of background I have played Far Cry 3 and Blood Dragons and have enjoyed both a lot.
In this game you will need to complete quests to level up and acquire new skills, and collect material from animals and plants to craft gear that you will need for harder quests. This is a core element to this series and is pretty enjoyable.
Right now I would give this game a 3.5 or 4/5  simply because of how riddled with bugs it is.
Here are a few examples of the bugs that I have explerienced throughout my gameplay.
1. As you clear caves/areas animals can still spawn behind you as you are leaving caves, other areas etc. Maybe not a bug but annoying spawn mechanics.
2. Animals can spawn behind objects, like a big rock lets say, that are as little as 1-2 meters away from you, even if you do approch slowly while crouched sometimes this does not work.
I know those first two are not really bugs however the next two are pretty game breaking.
3. Sabertooth taming. I have tamed quite a few now, and have had some die do to well, me letting them die while I take an outpost. That's fine, cool mechanics. What's not fine is how the last few I have tamed either disapear/die unexpectedly (know time to give them meat to revive, they are just dead between rocks, almost like it got stuck in the map) or worse are no longer tamed and will kill NPCs while I am questing. Not so fun.
4. As I was exploring a cave to pickup a Daysha hand, my back was up against a cave wall and the game pushed me under the cave wall texture, luckily there was water also in this texture area so I could drown myself and respawn at the nearest camp. Good thing I wasn't playing the mode where you die permanently huh? No wonder their Achievement says "no one can do this".
I know this is probably nit picking but I expect more for Ubisoft and the Far Cry series.

tl;dr  It's a semi-complete Far Cry game, only get it if you're a fan of the series or at a deep discount.
Pros:
+ It looks good, especially if you can put everything on higher settings.
+ Beast Hunting missions are really, really well done, as is the beast taming skill.
Cons:
- The storyline is very basic.  You're just building people huts, doing their missions, and eventually killing two bosses.  Most of the main missions feel more like side missions in other games.  There aren't any memorable characters like Vaas or Pagan Min.
- This is Crafting: The Game.  Everything needs crafting materials, from quest giver huts, to weapon designs, to ammo.  I thought I would enjoy it at first, but you are constantly needing to pick up rocks and sticks for the entire game.  Far Cry has always had problems with difficulty scaling, where if you do a lot of crafting the game quickly becomes very easy.  Primal is worse in that you can go from 'unable to kill a wolf' to crafting the final versions of one-hit-kill weapons in literally 30 minutes of gathering.
- Environments are a bit boring, just forests and colder mountain areas.
Conclusion:
Primal wasn't bad, but it's essentially a 'rental', something you can blow through in one weekend and never think of again.  I wish they had spent more time on the story (dunno what kind of story I was expecting with cavemen, but there you have it).

Yes, it is outrageous.
Yes, it is asinine.
Yes, it is unorthodox.
Yes, it is kinky.
Yes, it is crazy in more ways than you can possibly imagine.
Some of you believe SR has taken a turn for the worse, given that it used to be about the Saints' struggle against other gangs and striving to be at the top. Yes, the game lacks realism. The game doesn't seem to sport much sense, but it has fun acknowledging the fact that it is off-the-wall. They released a million dollar version of it in real life just to drag the insanity into the real world.
I bought the game when it initially came out, midnight release. I bought it here due to losing the game a while back, and obviously because the game was on offer at the time.
I enjoyed it back then, I'm enjoying it now. Romancing friends a la Mass Effect, text adventures akin to the earliest days in gaming, multiple references to other games, basically. (I particularly enjoyed seeing Kinzie attempt to use noclip.)
With dozens of activities, lots of DLC, a compelling, albeit nuts story, you'll be hard-pressed to find a more enjoyable game.
I do miss the days of the original Saints Row with a highly-immersive online mode, even Saints Row 2's online mode was something, at least. I do hope they look to include a bigger online mode with any future SR titles. Might attract even more people to this brilliant franchise.

is an open world zombie game wherein the balance between smashing faces with pipes and becoming a trapeze artist are equally important.
What took me by surprise initially was how much time I spent avoiding zombies entirely. I truly was expecting to smash every face I saw. This dichotomy is extremely well balanced; jumping around and climbing goes into a skill tree. Attacking and fighting nets you points for a separate skill tree. Now, you aren't building a character by any stretch. You essentially are only selecting the order in which you earn new abilities.
The sound design is excellent; from environmental screams to meaty bone crunching face smashing with crowbars everything feels very visceral and eerily tense. Even the air drops and planes flying overhead sound extremely close and create a sort of event in the environment. A sort of race for supplies.
Now, like all zombie themed things. Rarely is the narrative about the zombies themselves. It's far more intriguing to see how relationships develop between those that survive. One of the unique things about Harran (the city the game takes place in) is money still has value and this through me for a loop until I discovered that indeed the virus had been successfully quarantined and that this was all self contained.
I mentioned it was interesting to see how relationships develop. Well, as you might expect there are some folks that are less than decent; lets call it cordial. In the early game it's basically all melee but guns do indeed exist and once you start dealing with thugs from other groups of survivors guns become much more of a feasible option. Also, after you level your agility up, you gain the ability to use a grappling hook which is very nice as there is no fast travel whatsoever. This has the hidden ability to basically “Just Cause” yourself into the ground removing fall damage completely.
As an example, fighting some thugs in a, lets say 4v1 fight is definitely a white knuckle experience. Especially in close quarters. So much so that after that fight is over, traversing around the normal “biters” as the traditional slow basically lobotomized zombie has been deemed almost feels relaxing.
There are random events and side quests rampant throughout the city. There is almost too much content. The enhanced edition has even more and is almost a bit overwhelming.

If you love Cricket, stats and looking for that next star player then this is the game for you!
I've played Cricket Captain since 2001 when my cousin introduced me to it and have loved its simple interface and decent match engine since then.  It has had fairly minor tweaks over the years as my original tactics used to dominate one dayers dont work anymore and of course 20/20s arent all that old.
This game brings back memories...I played the first copy that I had to death and found a spreadsheet on an old usb that had stats for an England Captain game from 2000 to 2026 on it earlier today!  I've also bought a version that had Phil Hughes on the cover that I remember he averaged 65ish opening for Australia (might have been 2009?) as well as the 2011, 13 & 14 versions.  This is the best of the lot with the different game modes and a one-day engine that I haven't figured out yet (I'm only 30 odd hours in).
There is a reason I keep spreadsheets with this game - it has 1 big bug....at the end of the season some players may disappear!  It's something that's happened since the first version and with Nathan Lyon magically disappearing and taking his 176 wickets @ 31 as Australia's only spinner with him in 2015 I certainly noticed (particularly as Ryan Harris just retired and I lost 1/2 my bowling attack in 1 off season)....it's a worry when Maxwell is your frontline spinner!
It's sheer playability and the constant searching for that next great player helps to get over any quirks in the match engine as pretty much anything can be chalked up to it being cricket (still not sure how I got rolled for 50 in a T20 and then won the world cup only a couple of months later).
Just like Football Manager you'll make attachments to players you've never heard of...I see from my original game Matthew Bulbeck played 176 tests scoring 6898 runs at 36.11 and took 754 wickets at 28.65 (I'm sure he wouldn't have minded that sort of career and I've tried with Butterworth and Faulkner in recent years to find a similarly performing left handed allrounder) while I had a regen, G Fuller play 207 tests, score 20155 runs @ 70.97 with a HS of 397 and 75 100s.
In this years game I'm only up to 2016/17 with Australia but Chris Lynn 19 tests 1459 runs @  54.04, Ryan Carters 21 tests 1314 runs @ 50.54 and Glenn Maxwell 17 tests 808 runs @ 42.53, 35 wickets @ 35.23 would be pretty happy with their new careers!

My all time favourite is now on Steam! :D I used to play Quake Live now and then, but everyone was playing Clan Arena (team last man standing, like Counter Strike). I could not really enjoy that mode, so eventually I quit.  Now it's back with a few modifications.
The biggest change is a positive one imo: you get to start out with 2 weapons of your choice with a little bit of ammo. This solves the problem of getting spawnkilled all the time because you only have the machine gun (and the gauntlet) and the enemy has a fully loaded rocket launcher, lightning gun and heavy armor. At least now you are able to defend yourself with your weapon of choice and it allows you to jump straight into the action.
Finding a game is even easier than it was before: just pick form a category you want to play and it will find a game for you (a la Team Fortress). It seems all the game modes are now accessible for everyone (including Freeze Tag, yay!). There are some new game modes from Q3: Team Arena, such as Red Rover and Harvester.
I guess the community will get quite an influx of newbs, but that is fine (more fragfood, heh), at least people are still playing Q3. This is just the uncomplicated multiplayer fun I was looking for. No unlockable weapons/perks, no hats, no (god forbid) pay-to-win; just the old-skool fragging.

This game features a alien invaded world. Of couse that sounds like the common typical "alien invasion. End of days." Stop right there. You are wrong. The game itself features a very tactical strategy landscaped game. It comes with 4 difficulties; Easy, Normal, Classic, Impossible. You can also tweak the settings to use other features, such as "Ironman Mode" Which means you play on one continued save. No loading back. As far as the actual gameplay goes, you've got yourself a strategic plament game, sort of like chess. You have to move your troops into the rigth position, every decision you make could very well be your last, and also a game over. You have to upgrade your equipment well enough to fend off the aliens that threaten your race, by researching or crafting weapons and armor to do just that. But of course once you feel strong enough to handle a few minor aliens, that's when the aliens step up their game and throw in some other aliens that could ruin your day, or take out your whole squad with a single blow to each individual member. The very thought of one of your members being gunned and shot down basically has you sitting on the edge of your seat, desperatley hoping that your troop would be able to survive. And if there is no hope you could always flee. But the adventure doesn't even end there. It starts with you. Get this game. 10/10

Don't get this expecting a full game. It's roughly a DLC, but the intro to the story is bundled in with the main game (the two Special episodes), so it gains an Arcade mode to add a bit of substance. A word of warning: for about the first third of the game, I was worried that it was utterly, inexplicably terrible. Luckily, it's not. It is, though, mediocre, a bit tedious, and lacks the charm and depth of the original.
The quickest way to explain it, in my mind, is that it feels like it was made by a different group with different priorities. Manuscript pages now unlock weapons, for no particularly well-defined reason. Ammo caches are scattered around the map, but this leads to some oddly low caps for items (5 flares, 5 flashbangs, 10 batteries). There's a bit more of an open-world feel, but the areas are small (you don't get a map, and realistically don't need one) and it leads to a lot of ugly invisible walls. There's a nice variety of new enemies, but generic enemies are basically all you fight (no 'boss battles' and just a few poltergeists). The villain is a fairly interesting character, but it feels like he doesn't really get his chance to shine (er, no pun intended - his TV bits are reasonably well done but his short appearances ingame are underwhelming).
Now, most of these are tradeoffs - there's plenty that's different, but it's not objectively worse. The real problem, as far as I'm concerned, is that the story and the overall flow of the game - which are pretty directly connected - just don't work this time around, certainly not in the way that they did so well in the original.
The entire game takes place in three areas, each of which has a living population of precisely one attractive woman, which considering that in theory Wake is doing all the writing is more than a bit weird (there's arguably an excuse for him, but then there's not for the developers). The central mechanic of properly 'setting up' significant story points from the manuscript is actually pretty neat, but it's hamstrung by another central mechanic which isn't explained well, runs contrary to the concept of Wake having to write a coherent story, and leads to a lot of the gameplay feeling like doing the same thing over and over again in a way that isn't particularly interesting.
If you're looking for some more refined Alan Wake gameplay, this is a neat little DLC. If you're looking for a worthy continuation of the story, you might actually want to stay away. Overall, I'll give it a hesitant recommendation; there's a decent game under it all - it's just not Alan Wake.

Though not as engrossing as the original, American Nightmare is still good and acts as a pseudo sequel that continues the plight of our writer hero Alan Wake, as he attempts to make it back to our reality after having saved his wife from the darkness beneath Cauldron Lake two years ago only to be trapped within the realm of darkness himself. Furthermore, he faces off against his greatest foe, himself! Well, not really himself, rather his evil, dark twin Mr. Scratch who managed to escape into our reality from the dark realm.
This game is much heavier on action, as such there is now an arcade action mode that has you facing off against hordes of the Taken until the sun rises, that's assuming that you last that long. The story mode is short but sweet and collecting the manuscript pages allows you to unlock more powerful weapons than those you're used to, such as an assault rifle and combat shotgun.
Though this will likely leave most Wake fans desparately wanting a true follow up to the first game, it's still worth checking out when you have the time.

This is pretty much a Sims City type game of build and manage. The Central American Junta theme is a flavour, and I am not sure if it really impacts the game as much as I think it should.
This game has you balancing your International friends like USA, USSR, China, the Middle East and the EU, with some decisions you have to make. However, I think it is way too easy to play a non-aligned faction and pretty much please everybody.
Likewise, there are internal political factions to juggle, the Capitalist, the Nationalists, the Workers, the Environmentalists, etc. Again, these factions are too easy to please all at the same time. Especially if you're making good money.
I believe it is because how pleased each nation or faction is with the player is based on a linear scale. It should be on a exponential scale, the happier they are, the harder it should be to make them even happier. Also, I feel that decisions should always have a price other than money. Pleasing the Environmentalists should not just cost me money, but should also make Capitalists and Nationalists angry at me. Everytime I export stuff to the USSR, I should make USA unhappy with me..
That is not to say that the game is not fun. The build and manage works great, you're constantly pressured with rising costs and a lack of skilled talent early on. And it is really fun, it is just that the Junta flavour is just that, flavour. They call you El Presidente in an accent and play Latin American music in the background, but they could do so much more with it. Being a non-aligned, centrist, highly profitable, benevolent leader should be a hard balance to achieve, not the default.
In closing, this is a fun and working build and manage game, but you have to inject your own drama by purposefully♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off factions and nations. Playing efficiently is the least interesting option.

I got this game as a gift but it really isnt worth the money in my opinion
Heres the main issues for me:
1. The game is fun until you hit the level 50 mark. then the game (for seemingly no reason) ramps up the time to level by a ridiculous amount. 1-50 takes about 4 hours of grinding if youre quick. Grinding from 50-56 takes about 6 hours. Yes you read that right. it takes 2 hours more to level 6 levels than it does to level 50. level 56+ is even more ridiculous in the time. If i kill 300 mobs why do i only go up 1% xp?
2. They don't really explain anything aside from how to move and attack. Leave it up to a game like this to give you all kinds of things to do while afk to get money, Except its ridiculously hard to do any of it. Hunting is the best example i can give of this. You think you would be able to shoot anything or they would even make the mobs that you CAN shoot actually able to be located? nope. as far as ive seen it doesnt specify anything as huntable. You have to just run around blindly until you accidentally stumble onto something that is shootable. And the map is massive so its not exactly an easy or even medium difficulty skill.
3. You MUST- I repeat MUST buy any item from the player marketplace at the lowest price. it doesnt let you buy anything that isnt the lowest priced item. Take beer for example. Beer is highly sought after in this game and it gets bought quickly. Well if theres 2 beers and one is 170k silver and one is 180k silver you are FORCED to buy/bid on the 170k one, As is everyone else. This only makes a system where its incredibly hard to buy common items. You get the message that you have to buy the lowest priced one, Click ok, go to buy the lowest priced one, SOLD OUT. Well ok you say as you hit the refresh button. To your surprise the item that you were told was sold out isnt. the exact listing you tried to buy is still there. If i want to pay the extra money for an item, I should be able to. And if the item you want is really widely demanded (such as Beer or Black Stones) the game will lag because of the amount of people buying the items so quickly. theres like a 1/1000000 chance youll end up acctually getting the chance to buy an item such as Beer before it sells out and the new wave of player stock is put up for bidding (which gets sold out as soon as bidding is over). I should add that bidding is different than what youre thinking of because bidding in this game isnt competitively placing money on an item until the time expires. No. Its instead a complete RNGfest in which you click the button and it says "bidding results" and you hope that maybe youre the one who gets the item out of the hundreds of others that are FORCED TO all bid on this same item.
I'd give it a 4/10.  Wouldnt recommend spending the 10 dollars on this. Go play a better mmo.

I honestly can't recommend this game.  It's not that it's a bad game, but the poker AI is just atrocious.  Here's a typical scenario:  I have pocket jacks pre-flop and I'm on the button.  First to act raises.  I re-raise.  Small blind goes all in.  Big blind goes all in.  First to raise goes all in.  I fold because in a real poker game, I'm guaranteed to be beat at this point.  They all turn over their cards: 10 4 off suit, 2 3 suited, and 8 5 off suit.  What the hell?!  This is not a realistic poker situation, even for beginners.  You would think playing people who are this reckless would be easy, but oh no!  Pretty much anytime I have a legit hand that I'm confident in, every single player will call my bets/ raises.  Consequently, the power of numbers works against me and the majority of the time the AI sucks out with a terrible hand.  And if you play tight, all that happens is that the other four players play reckless and they end up giving all of their chips to a single player who will now have a 4:1 stack lead over you.  That's pretty hard to overcome.  On the plus side, the animations are great and the conversation by the players is truly entertaining (minus Tycho, who comes across as extremely annoying).  If you're a fan of any of the characters/ franchises included in this game, I would recommend picking this up as that part is rather entertaining.  If you're looking for a good solid poker game however, I would avoid this as the AI is simply terrible and you will spend most of your time frustrated by it.  I would give this a 5.5/10.
